message.content: In domestic cats and many other felids, the presence of a mane (the long, shaggy fur that develops around the head and neck) is controlled by a dominant allele. In lions, the same principle applies: the gene that triggers the growth of a mane in males is dominant over the allele that would produce a non‑mane phenotype. Thus, if a lion inherits the “mane” allele from either parent, it will develop a mane—making this a classic example of a dominant genetic trait in the species.
